# Config reference

<!-- generated by scripts/gen_reference.py from the config classes;
     edit the docstrings and Field descriptions, not this page -->

A run config is one JSON file. Every field has a default, so `{}` is a
valid config; `seisbench-trainer config` prints the defaults and
`seisbench-trainer config run.json` checks a file and prints every
value it resolves to. A choice between alternatives (a dataset source,
a training step, an optimizer, ...) is an object whose `type` field
names the member, e.g. `{"type": "adam", "lr": 0.001}`.

## TrainConfig {#trainconfig}

One training run. Every field has a default, so ``{}`` is a valid
config; ``seisbench-trainer config`` prints them all.

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `data` | [DataConfig](#dataconfig) | [defaults](#dataconfig) | Datasets, component order, sampling rate and loaders. |
| `model` | [PhaseNetConfig](#phasenetconfig) | `{"type": "PhaseNet"}` | Picker model, its starting weights and its loss. |
| `augmentation` | [AugmentationConfig](#augmentationconfig) | [defaults](#augmentationconfig) | Training windows and perturbations, normalization and labels. |
| `training` | [TrainingConfig](#trainingconfig) | [defaults](#trainingconfig) | Training loop: length, seed, optimizer, scheduler, model selection. |
| `evaluation` | [EvaluationConfig](#evaluationconfig) | [defaults](#evaluationconfig) | Validation and test metrics, baseline model, figures. |
| `tracking` | [TrackingConfig](#trackingconfig) | [defaults](#trackingconfig) | MLflow experiment, run name and tags. |
| `hpo` | [HPOConfig](#hpoconfig) \| null | `null` | Hyperparameter search; used by the hpo command. |

## DataConfig {#dataconfig}

Datasets to load and how to load them.

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `datasets` | list[[SeisBenchDataset](#seisbenchdataset) \| [LocalDataset](#localdataset) \| [SyntheticDataset](#syntheticdataset)] | `[{"type": "seisbench", "name": "ETHZ"}]` | One or more datasets. Their splits are concatenated. |
| `component_order` | string | `"ZNE"` | Waveform component order the model is trained on. |
| `sampling_rate` | float (> 0) | `100.0` | In Hz. Every dataset is resampled to it on access; the pick sample columns follow. |
| `resample_zerophase` | bool | `true` | Zero-phase anti-alias filter when a dataset is decimated (seisbench's default is causal, which delays the waveforms against the picks). True matches the default of the models' annotate, so training and inference see the same filter. |
| `batch_size` | int (> 0) | `1024` | Windows per batch, in training and evaluation. |
| `num_workers` | int (> 0) | `8` | DataLoader workers. Must be at least 1. |

## SeisBenchDataset {#seisbenchdataset}

Select with `"type": "seisbench"`.

A dataset class from ``seisbench.data``, downloaded on first use.

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | string | required | Class name in seisbench.data, e.g. 'ETHZ'. |
| `query` | string \| null | `null` | Optional pandas query on the metadata to select traces, e.g. "source_magnitude &gt; 1". |
| `preprocessing` | list[[Filter](#filter) \| [Resplit](#resplit)] | `[]` | Steps applied in order after the query and before the dataset is split: filter, resplit. |

## Filter {#filter}

Select with `"type": "filter"`.

Keep the traces of ``splits`` that match ``query``; other splits stay whole.

For example, ``trace_category == "noise"`` on ``["train"]`` trains on
noise only while validation and test keep every trace.

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `query` | string | required | Pandas query on the metadata; matching traces are kept, e.g. 'trace_category == "noise"'. |
| `splits` | list[`"train"` \| `"dev"` \| `"test"`] | `["train", "dev", "test"]` | Splits the filter acts on, by the metadata 'split' column as it is at this step. |

## Resplit {#resplit}

Select with `"type": "resplit"`.

Overwrite the metadata 'split' column with a seeded random assignment.

Traces that share a ``group_by`` value (by default the event,
``source_id``) always land in the same split, so that one event recorded
at many stations does not appear in both training and test. Traces
without a group value (noise) are assigned one by one. Whole groups are
shuffled and assigned in turn, so the trace fractions hold up to the size
of one group. The result depends only on the seed and the metadata.

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `fractions` | dict[str, float (>= 0, <= 1)] | required | Share of the traces per split, summing to 1. A missing split gets no traces. |
| `seed` | int (>= 0) | `0` | Fixes the split; independent of training.seed, so that runs with different training seeds share one test set. |
| `group_by` | string \| null | `"source_id"` | Metadata column whose traces stay together. None assigns every trace on its own. |

## LocalDataset {#localdataset}

Select with `"type": "local"`.

A SeisBench-format dataset in a local directory.

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `path` | path | required | Directory with metadata.csv and waveforms.hdf5; ~ is the home directory. |
| `query` | string \| null | `null` | Optional pandas query on the metadata to select traces. |
| `preprocessing` | list[[Filter](#filter) \| [Resplit](#resplit)] | `[]` | Steps applied in order after the query and before the dataset is split: filter, resplit. |

## SyntheticDataset {#syntheticdataset}

Select with `"type": "synthetic"`.

Generated test data (noise plus P and S wavelets); no download needed.

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `n_traces` | int (> 0) | `300` | Number of traces. |
| `trace_length_s` | float (>= 30) | `60.0` | Length of every trace. |
| `sampling_rate` | float (> 0) | `100.0` | Rate the traces are written at, in Hz. |
| `noise_fraction` | float (>= 0, < 1) | `0.1` | Share of pure noise traces. |
| `seed` | int (>= 0) | `0` | Seed of the generator; fixes the dataset. |
| `query` | string \| null | `null` | Optional pandas query on the metadata to select traces. |
| `preprocessing` | list[[Filter](#filter) \| [Resplit](#resplit)] | `[]` | Steps applied in order after the query and before the dataset is split: filter, resplit. |

## PhaseNetConfig {#phasenetconfig}

Select with `"type": "PhaseNet"`.

PhaseNet (Zhu & Beroza 2019): a U-Net with softmax outputs for P, S and
noise. Input 3001 samples (30 s at 100 Hz) unless
``augmentation.window_s`` sets another length.

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `pretrained` | string \| null | `null` | Weights to start from: a SeisBench pretrained name (e.g. 'original') or a local SeisBench model: the path of its .json (or .pt) file, or that path without suffix. None trains from scratch. |
| `sampling_rate` | float (> 0) \| null | `null` | Run pretrained weights at this rate instead of their own: data at this rate is fed as if it were at the original rate, which stretches time by original/new (a 100 Hz PhaseNet at 50 Hz sees 3001 samples = 60 s). The exported model stores it, so annotate and qseek resample their input to it. Must equal data.sampling_rate. None keeps the weights' own rate. |
| `loss` | [CrossEntropyLoss](#crossentropyloss) | `{"type": "cross_entropy"}` | Training loss on the model's logits. |

## CrossEntropyLoss {#crossentropyloss}

Select with `"type": "cross_entropy"`.

Soft-target cross-entropy over the softmax output channels (PhaseNet).

Per sample, ``-sum_c w_c * y_c * log(q_c)``; averaged over the samples
and the batch, leaving out the samples where the batch's ``label_mask``
(``augmentation.missing_picks``) marks an unread phase. The default takes
``log_softmax`` of the logits, as the original PhaseNet, and weighs the
noise channel 0.5. ``from_logits=False``
and ``weights={}`` give SeisBench's pick-benchmark ``vector_cross_entropy``
(``log(softmax + eps)``, unweighted).

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `weights` | dict[str, float (>= 0)] | `{"N": 0.5}` | Weight per output channel, by label; missing channels weigh 1. The default N 0.5 balances P and S against the far more frequent noise samples: on BohemiaSaxony it gave the best F1 and pick times. |
| `from_logits` | bool | `true` | True takes log_softmax of the logits (numerically stable, as in the original PhaseNet). False takes log(softmax + eps), as in SeisBench's pick-benchmark. |
| `eps` | float (> 0) | `1e-05` | Added to the softmax when from_logits is false. |

## AugmentationConfig {#augmentationconfig}

Training augmentations, normalization and labels. Durations in seconds.

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `train` | list[[PickWindow](#pickwindow) \| [RandomWindow](#randomwindow) \| [ChannelDropout](#channeldropout) \| [AddGap](#addgap) \| [GaussianNoise](#gaussiannoise) \| [RotateHorizontal](#rotatehorizontal) \| [RealNoise](#realnoise)] | `pick_window`, `random_window`, `rotate_horizontal`, `real_noise`, `channel_dropout` | Training pipeline, applied in order: pick_window steps, exactly one random_window crop to the model input length, then the perturbations. Validation and test use fixed windows instead. |
| `window_s` | float (> 0) \| null | `null` | Model input length. None uses the model's own input length. |
| `normalization` | `"peak"` \| `"std"` | `"std"` | Per channel, after the training steps and in evaluation alike. PhaseNet then normalizes each channel again by its own ``norm`` (annotate_batch_pre), as at inference, so for PhaseNet this does not change the model input. |
| `label_sigma_s` | float (> 0) | `0.1` | Width of the pick label curve. |
| `label_shape` | `"gaussian"` \| `"triangle"` \| `"box"` | `"gaussian"` | Shape of the label curve around a pick: Gaussian with std label_sigma_s, triangle or box with half-width label_sigma_s. |
| `max_sp_s` | float (> 0) \| null | `15.0` | Longest S-P time. With missing_picks='unread', an event's unread P is looked for only this far before its S, and an unread S this far after its P, instead of up to the window edge, which in a multi-event window would also hide the other events' arrivals from the loss. None: up to the window edge. The default suits local and volcanic seismicity (99.9 % of the S-P times below 14.7 s on BohemiaSaxony, 12 s on deeplowfrequency); raise it for regional data. |
| `label_events` | `"trace_event"` \| `"all_events"` | `"all_events"` | Whose arrivals are labelled, and scored in validation and test. 'trace_event': only the event the trace was cut for (its metadata row; seisbench's behaviour). 'all_events': also every other event recorded at the same station with an arrival inside the trace, so that in a swarm the other events are not labelled noise and their detections not counted as false picks (docs/experiments.md, 2026-11-17: better F1, pick times and qseek catalogues). Needs trace_start_time, trace_sampling_rate_hz and the station codes in the metadata; set 'trace_event' for a dataset without them. |
| `missing_picks` | `"unread"` \| `"absent"` | `"unread"` | What a missing P or S pick means on a trace that has a pick of the other phase. 'unread' (as in the DLF v4b training): the analyst did not read it, but the arrival may be there. Where it can be, the training loss ignores all output channels and the validation and test metrics ignore that phase's peaks: before the first S pick if P is missing, after the first P pick if S is missing, each with a margin of 3 label_sigma_s. Otherwise the model would learn 'no P' before S on S-only traces (65 % of the Japan traces) and be scored down for picking it. 'absent': a missing pick means no arrival; the label is noise there and every peak of that phase is a false pick (seisbench pick-benchmark). Traces without any pick are noise in both. |

## PickWindow {#pickwindow}

Select with `"type": "pick_window"`.

Cut a context window around a random pick (``WindowAroundSample``).

Applied with ``probability``; otherwise the following ``random_window``
crops from the whole trace, which may then contain no pick at all.

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `probability` | float (>= 0, <= 1) | required | Chance that the step is applied to a training example. |
| `length_s` | float (> 0) | `60.0` | Window length. |
| `before_s` | float (>= 0) | `30.0` | Window start before the selected pick. |

## RandomWindow {#randomwindow}

Select with `"type": "random_window"`.

Crop a random window of the model input length; pad short traces.

Always applied; exactly one per pipeline.

## ChannelDropout {#channeldropout}

Select with `"type": "channel_dropout"`.

Zero a random subset of the channels: at least one, never all.

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `probability` | float (>= 0, <= 1) | required | Chance that the step is applied to a training example. |

## AddGap {#addgap}

Select with `"type": "add_gap"`.

Zero all channels over a stretch (a data gap); picks in it are dropped.

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `probability` | float (>= 0, <= 1) | required | Chance that the step is applied to a training example. |
| `length_s` | tuple[float (>= 0), float (>= 0)] | `[0.5, 5.0]` | Gap length range. EQTransformer used gaps of up to 5 s. |

## GaussianNoise {#gaussiannoise}

Select with `"type": "gaussian_noise"`.

Add white noise; its std is ``scale`` times the waveform peak.

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `probability` | float (>= 0, <= 1) | required | Chance that the step is applied to a training example. |
| `scale` | tuple[float (>= 0), float (>= 0)] | `[0.0, 0.15]` | Noise std relative to the absolute peak of the waveform. |

## RotateHorizontal {#rotatehorizontal}

Select with `"type": "rotate_horizontal"`.

Rotate N and E by a random angle in [-pi, pi).

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `probability` | float (>= 0, <= 1) | required | Chance that the step is applied to a training example. |

## RealNoise {#realnoise}

Select with `"type": "real_noise"`.

Add a random window of a recorded noise trace from the training split.

The noise's horizontal components are rotated by a random angle first.
Windows without a pick (noise traces, pick-free crops) get no noise, so
``probability`` is the chance per window with a pick. If ``query``
selects no training traces (or names a missing column), the step logs a
warning and adds nothing.

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `probability` | float (>= 0, <= 1) | required | Chance that the step is applied to a training example. |
| `query` | string | `"trace_category == \"noise\""` | Pandas query on the training split metadata that selects the noise traces. Dev and test traces are never used. |
| `level` | [PeakRatio](#peakratio) \| [StdRatio](#stdratio) | `{"type": "peak"}` | How loud the noise is relative to the window: 'peak' (noise peak 0-1 times the window peak) or 'std' (the dlf-catalog reference: noise std 0.1-2 times the window std, log-uniform). |

## PeakRatio {#peakratio}

Select with `"type": "peak"`.

Noise peak = ``ratio`` times the window's absolute peak (seisbench's
``scaling_type="peak"``); ``ratio`` drawn uniformly. Peaks are over all
channels, so the ratio depends on how impulsive the event is.

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `ratio` | tuple[float (>= 0), float (>= 0)] | `[0.0, 1.0]` | (low, high) of the peak ratio. |

## StdRatio {#stdratio}

Select with `"type": "std"`.

Noise std = ``ratio`` times the window's std, ``ratio`` drawn
log-uniformly (uniform in dB); all-zero channels are left out of the std.
The dlf-catalog reference recipe: ratio 0.1 to 2.

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `ratio` | tuple[float (>= 0), float (>= 0)] | `[0.1, 2.0]` | (low, high) of the std ratio; both above 0. |

## TrainingConfig {#trainingconfig}

Training loop. By default every run finds its own length: the plateau
scheduler halves the learning rate after 5 epochs without improvement and
early stopping ends the run after 15; ``epochs`` is only the limit.

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `epochs` | int (> 0) | `100` | Upper limit; early stopping usually ends the run sooner. |
| `seed` | int | `42` | Seeds weights, the training augmentations and the fixed validation and test windows. Runs with the same config and seed are reproducible; compare settings with two seeds (run-to-run noise of det/f1_mean is about 0.002). |
| `accelerator` | `"auto"` \| `"cpu"` \| `"gpu"` | `"auto"` | Lightning accelerator; a run always uses one device. 'auto' takes the GPU if there is one. |
| `precision` | `"32-true"` \| `"16-mixed"` \| `"bf16-mixed"` | `"32-true"` | Lightning precision. Mixed precision is faster on GPUs but has not been compared against 32-true. |
| `monitor` | `"val_loss"` \| `"det/f1_mean"` \| `"det_P/f1"` \| `"det_S/f1"` | `"det/f1_mean"` | Validation metric that picks the best model: checkpointing, early stopping, the plateau scheduler, HPO and the registry. val_loss is minimized, the F1 scores are maximized. |
| `early_stopping_patience` | int (> 0) \| null | `15` | Stop after this many epochs without improvement. None disables it (needed for the cosine scheduler). |
| `min_delta` | float (>= 0) | `0.002` | Smallest change of monitor that counts as an improvement, for early stopping and the plateau scheduler. 0.002 is the run-to-run noise of det/f1_mean on BohemiaSaxony; use about 0.0005 for val_loss. |
| `optimizer` | [AdamConfig](#adamconfig) \| [AdamWConfig](#adamwconfig) | `{"type": "adam"}` | Optimizer and its learning rate ('adam' or 'adamw'). |
| `scheduler` | [CosineConfig](#cosineconfig) \| [PlateauConfig](#plateauconfig) \| [ExponentialConfig](#exponentialconfig) \| null | `{"type": "plateau"}` | Learning-rate schedule. None keeps the rate constant. |
| `checkpoint_dir` | path | `"checkpoints"` | Local or scratch directory for Lightning checkpoints. They are not uploaded to MLflow. |

## AdamConfig {#adamconfig}

Select with `"type": "adam"`.

Adam. The default rate 0.001 tied the alternatives when fine-tuning;
the BohemiaSaxony runs from scratch used 0.003.

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `lr` | float (> 0) | `0.001` | Initial learning rate. |
| `weight_decay` | float (>= 0) | `0.0` | L2 penalty, added to the gradients. |

## AdamWConfig {#adamwconfig}

Select with `"type": "adamw"`.

AdamW: Adam with decoupled weight decay.

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `lr` | float (> 0) | `0.001` | Initial learning rate. |
| `weight_decay` | float (>= 0) | `0.01` | Decoupled weight decay per step. |

## CosineConfig {#cosineconfig}

Select with `"type": "cosine"`.

Cosine annealing over all training epochs.

Needs a fixed length: disable early stopping (it would end the run while
the rate is still high) and set ``training.epochs`` to the length found
with the plateau default.

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `eta_min` | float (>= 0) | `0.0` | Learning rate at the last epoch. |

## PlateauConfig {#plateauconfig}

Select with `"type": "plateau"`.

Reduce the learning rate when ``training.monitor`` stops improving.

An epoch counts as an improvement only if it beats the best value by
``training.min_delta``, as for early stopping. With early stopping, set
``patience`` below the early-stopping patience, so the rate drops before
the run ends.

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `factor` | float (> 0, < 1) | `0.5` | Learning-rate factor per drop. |
| `patience` | int (>= 0) | `5` | Epochs without improvement before the rate drops. 5 against early stopping's 15 leaves several drops before a run ends. |

## ExponentialConfig {#exponentialconfig}

Select with `"type": "exponential"`.

Multiply the learning rate by ``decay`` after every epoch.

AI4EPS PhaseNet decays Adam's rate (0.01) by 0.9 per epoch (staircase
``exponential_decay`` with one epoch of steps).

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `decay` | float (> 0, <= 1) | `0.9` | Learning-rate factor per epoch. |

## EvaluationConfig {#evaluationconfig}

Validation and test evaluation. Durations in seconds.

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `pick_window_s` | float (> 0) | `2.0` | Half-width of the window around the expected pick for the pick-accuracy metrics. |
| `tolerance_s` | float (> 0) | `0.5` | Matching tolerance of the detection metrics. |
| `test_tolerances_s` | list[float (> 0)] | `[0.1, 0.2, 0.5]` | Matching tolerances of the test evaluation (one set of scores each) and of the 'within_&lt;t&gt;s' pick-accuracy fractions. |
| `min_peak_height` | float (> 0, < 1) | `0.05` | Lowest probability peak that counts as a detection; the threshold curves start above it. |
| `min_peak_distance_s` | float (> 0) | `1.0` | Closer peaks of one phase are merged into the higher one. |
| `edge_mask_s` | float (>= 0) | `1.0` | Samples this close to the trace edges are ignored for noise scores. |
| `baseline` | [PhaseNetConfig](#phasenetconfig) \| null | `{"type": "PhaseNet", "pretrained": "original"}` | Pretrained model evaluated alongside for comparison, fed in its own component order. None disables the baseline. |
| `noisy_validation` | [NoisyValidation](#noisyvalidation) \| null | [defaults](#noisyvalidation) | Also validate on the dev windows with real noise from the dev split's noise traces added (metrics 'noisy/...'). Skipped if the dev split has no noise traces. None disables it. |
| `plot_every_n_epochs` | int (>= 0) | `1` | 0 disables the figures. |
| `test_at_end` | bool | `false` | Evaluate the best model and the baseline on the test split after training (thresholds from the dev split). HPO trials never do. |

## NoisyValidation {#noisyvalidation}

A second validation pass: the same dev windows with real noise added.

The noise comes from the dev split's own noise traces, which training
never sees, and is added as by ``real_noise`` (horizontals rotated, only
to windows with a pick), seeded per trace: every epoch and every run with
the same seed gets the same noisy windows. Its metrics carry the prefix
``noisy/``; model selection and thresholds stay on the clean windows.

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `query` | string | `"trace_category == \"noise\""` | Pandas query on the dev split metadata that selects the noise traces. Without matches the noisy validation is skipped. |
| `level` | [PeakRatio](#peakratio) \| [StdRatio](#stdratio) | `{"type": "peak", "ratio": [0.5, 1.0]}` | Noise level, drawn per trace. Default: noise peak 0.5-1 times the window peak, the harder half of real_noise's default. |

## TrackingConfig {#trackingconfig}

Where the run is logged. The tracking server or folder comes from the
MLFLOW_TRACKING_URI environment variable, not from the config.

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `experiment` | string \| null | `null` | MLflow experiment. None derives it from datasets and model. |
| `run_name` | string \| null | `null` | MLflow run name. None lets MLflow pick one. |
| `tags` | dict[str, string] | `{}` | Extra MLflow run tags, e.g. {"purpose": "lr-grid"}. |

## HPOConfig {#hpoconfig}

Hyperparameter search with Optuna (the optional hpo extra). Every
trial is a full training run with the sampled values applied.

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `study_name` | string | required | Optuna study, shared by all workers; also the MLflow parent run name (hpo-&lt;study&gt;). |
| `storage` | path | `"optuna.journal"` | Optuna journal file, shared by all workers of the study (on the shared filesystem on a cluster). |
| `n_trials` | int (> 0) | `20` | Total number of trials over all workers. |
| `sampler` | [TPEConfig](#tpeconfig) \| [RandomConfig](#randomconfig) | `{"type": "tpe"}` | How trials draw values. |
| `pruner` | [MedianConfig](#medianconfig) \| [HyperbandConfig](#hyperbandconfig) \| null | `{"type": "median"}` | Stops weak trials early on training.monitor. None never prunes. |
| `params` | list[[FloatParam](#floatparam) \| [IntParam](#intparam) \| [CategoricalParam](#categoricalparam)] | required | The search space. The data and the objective are fixed: data.datasets, data.component_order, data.sampling_rate, augmentation.label_events and training.monitor cannot be tuned. |

## TPEConfig {#tpeconfig}

Select with `"type": "tpe"`.

Tree-structured Parzen estimator (Optuna's default).

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `n_startup_trials` | int (>= 0) | `10` | Random trials before TPE takes over. |
| `seed` | int \| null | `null` | Sampler seed; None draws one. |

## RandomConfig {#randomconfig}

Select with `"type": "random"`.

Independent random sampling.

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `seed` | int \| null | `null` | Sampler seed; None draws one. |

## MedianConfig {#medianconfig}

Select with `"type": "median"`.

Prune a trial below the median of earlier trials at the same epoch.

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `n_startup_trials` | int (>= 0) | `5` | Trials that are never pruned. |
| `n_warmup_steps` | int (>= 0) | `5` | Epochs before a trial can be pruned. |

## HyperbandConfig {#hyperbandconfig}

Select with `"type": "hyperband"`.

Hyperband: successive halving over several brackets.

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `min_resource` | int (> 0) | `1` | Fewest epochs before a trial can be pruned. |
| `reduction_factor` | int (>= 2) | `3` | Share of trials kept per rung: 1 / factor. |

## FloatParam {#floatparam}

Select with `"type": "float"`.

A float drawn from [low, high].

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `path` | string | required | Dotted config path, e.g. 'training.optimizer.lr'; list items by index. |
| `low` | float | required | Smallest value. |
| `high` | float | required | Largest value. |
| `log` | bool | `false` | Sample on a log scale (rates, decays). |
| `step` | float (> 0) \| null | `null` | Grid step; None samples continuously. |

## IntParam {#intparam}

Select with `"type": "int"`.

An integer drawn from [low, high].

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `path` | string | required | Dotted config path, e.g. 'data.batch_size'. |
| `low` | int | required | Smallest value. |
| `high` | int | required | Largest value. |
| `log` | bool | `false` | Sample on a log scale. |
| `step` | int (> 0) | `1` | Grid step. |

## CategoricalParam {#categoricalparam}

Select with `"type": "categorical"`.

One of a list of scalars. Switch a union member by its type field,
e.g. path 'training.optimizer.type' with choices ['adam', 'adamw'].

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `path` | string | required | Dotted config path. |
| `choices` | list[string \| int \| float \| bool \| null] | required | The candidates. |
